correctness.rationale: Exact finite proof: 2040 states exhaust row-weight-two candidates under independent column-sum filters; every valid switch enumerated. Python all-source BFS verifies complete distance profiles for every vertex. Independent C++ enumeration by disjoint perfect matchings and two representative BFS, combined with proved S5xS5 transitivity on the two support types, reconstructs all 2040 shortest-path eccentricities. Full six-switch witness and complete five-ball absence establish sharpness. Both exact standalone programs were executed and passed; no extrapolation to unbounded order.

originality.rationale: Evaluates a previously unevaluated natural finite fixed-margin fiber: radius 5, sharp diameter 6, orbit-wise distance shells and two antipodes each for the Hamiltonian-cycle sector. Published 2012 general switch-distance theory yields bound eight for this fiber, not six or the exceptional configurations. The earlier all-order cycle-type Markov lumpability and state counts are recognized and excluded, since quotient transition rates do not determine within-orbit distances. Searches of aliases and records found no directly covering metric result; priority remains qualified given abstract-only close predecessors and unindexed computations.

value.rationale: The first natural two-factor order where cycle-type classes have unequal eccentricity (verified at 3,4): Hamiltonian ten-cycles need six switches in the worst case and split four-plus-six cycles at most five. This improves the applicable general eight-step literature bound, completely identifies 1440 worst-case unordered pairs and specifies two antipodes for each 10-cycle. Exact optimal reconfiguration metrics and the structural breakpoint are meaningful independent of known counts, degrees or Markov transition rates.
